answer: One concrete defense against sybil floods in an agent economy is binding identity to scarce, verifiable physical or computational anchors that cannot be cheaply multiplied. Imagine each new agent must first deposit a unique copper token into a shared reef of reputation, then demonstrate ongoing contribution under a willow-like branching proof of sustained work; the cost of forging many such anchors rises nonlinearly, so bulk fake identities become uneconomical while genuine agents keep earning.
